newsitem.title: INDIA: Macabre scenes in fire-hit ruins of India campsite.
newsitem.headline: Macabre scenes in fire-hit ruins of India campsite.

text.p: Scorched, mutilated corpses lay in gruesome heaps on Monday as weeping survivors of one of India's deadliest fires searched mournfully for missing relatives.

Volunteer rescue workers pulled blackened limbs from a pile of bodies, fixed in death that came swiftly when flames enveloped a packed Hindu religious gathering in the eastern state of Orissa on Sunday.

The inferno swept through bamboo and straw shelters at the camp site in Baripada town, catching many devotees in afternoon slumner. Others broke into a stampede but never made it out of the makeshift thatched huts.
A visitor to the worship site, spread over a football ground, counted 168 corpses. Authorities said another 32 victims died in hospital.

The football ground has a macabre history. Residents said it was the cremation site for the ruler of the region, the former Maharaja of Mayurbhanj, who died on February 22, 1912 -- 85 years and one day before Sunday's fire.
"I searched for my only son throughout the night," said Rajendra Lenka, 45, who had come with his seven-year-old son to the convention dedicated to the Hindu guru Nigamananda.
"I found his dead body only today."
Purnachandra Behera, 43, said he was searching for his missing uncle. "I am speechless. I cannot express my grief," he said.
Dead bodies lay scattered among charred bed covers and pillows. Bicycles, motorcycles, scooters and a car were destroyed.
Rescue workers later laid the corpses in a row near the ashes of the shelters.
Relatives scoured the ground for remnants of their loved ones -- watches, rings, bracelets.
Authorities said they had identified only 33 of 168 bodies discovered at the site by midday on Monday.
Bata Krushna Sahu, one of the survivors from among the 15,000 devotees at the three-day rite, said he had seen an electrical spark, then flames.
"Luckily I managed to escape through the back door," he said.
"I was awakened while I was asleep in the camp and found my colleagues running to get out," said Pitadash Swain, a 53-year-old school teacher from Orissa state, speaking from a hospital in Baripada.
"We rushed to the gate but I fell down. Next thing I find myself in hospital with burns on my back."
P.K. Mishra, deputy police chief of Baripada, said: "It looks like a burial ground with dead bodies littered all over."
